One common way to measure the global trend in armed conflicts is to count annually the pairs of countries that are engaged in warfare with one another. The decades after World War II saw a wave of decolonization along with the collapse of the Soviet Empire in the 1990s, resulting in the number of sovereign countries growing from approximately 50 in 1946 to nearly 200 today.
